title: 中央纪年匾下最高一排四窗，2015与另一公开建筑史照片互核
frame: Local graphic proportions for the ornamental crown. The cartouche width is one display unit. X increases to illustration right and the common sill is the drawing baseline.
same_published_view_reprint: The 2015 reprint uses the same press photograph.

window_observations.hidden: Both upper corners behind the projecting shade, first photo and independent feature. Inferred from exposed jambs and neighbouring visible heads.

Opening perimeter visible. Lower corners of the third are partially overlapped by a brown lattice enclosure below it.

right_pair.upper_meeting_stiles: The lit top tier has dark edges around the central meeting stile. The exact rebate is below reliable photographic resolution.

steelwork.left_pair: A dark frame and a narrow horizontal division are visible under each shade. The concealed upper steel grid is unresolved.
steelwork.surface: Mid-brown brick, pale stone finish to the three thin facade fins and sills, dark grey fabric and a worn light hem on the two shades, pale blue-grey reflective panes in the unshaded frames. Brown perforated covers below the second and third openings are separately identified as later masking elements. No interior fixtures are required.

sources.label: Architectural history feature, crown photograph credited to original blog

additional_source.use: Two separate projecting shades with dark underside and rounded/sloping side profiles, the front hems are pale and slightly scalloped. Used only for the upper crown.

reading_method: The published crown photographs were compared for window families, glazing divisions, canvas shape and plaster or brick finishes. Dimensions describe the model in units of the dated plaque width. The two shaded windows have inferred head profiles.
uprights: Three pale upright stone strips separate the four openings. Their visible widths by the upper sills are approximately 0.06 of the cartouche width.
